holdings.thesis: HOLD, thesis reinforced: Q3 2026 results (reported before today's 10/30 open) showed adjusted EPS $4.23 (beat the ~$4.01-4.09 consensus) and revenue $110.5B (+29.6% YoY, above the ~$104.4B consensus), as the refining-margin tailwind (record refining utilization/crack spreads) offset the expected upstream liquids-price/Guyana-entitlement headwind, exactly the setup flagged going in. $25.7B operating cash flow, dividend raised 4%, and the $20B buyback pace confirmed to continue into 2027. Shares up ~1.9% to $186.82 on the print. Return +17.1%. Position ~13.8%.

HOLD, watch tightens: a wave of sell-side price-target cuts landed 10/29-10/30 reacting to the 10/28 Q3 report (KeyCorp to $385, Wells Fargo to $371, Citigroup to $375, BMO to $425 citing search-revenue miss and margin pressure, plus Cantor Fitzgerald, Piper Sandler, Truist, BofA, Wedbush, Morgan Stanley, RBC, DA Davidson) -- but nearly every firm kept its Buy/Overweight/Outperform rating, reading as 'estimates come down, thesis intact' rather than capitulation. Part of the EPS shortfall is attributed to a mark-to-market loss on Alphabet's SpaceX stake, not core operating weakness. Neither the stop-loss (-25%) nor the position cap is breached. Return -17.1%. Position ~13.3%.

HOLD, watch escalates: Q3 2026 results (reported 10/29 AMC) showed AWS reaccelerating sharply -- $45.98B revenue +39% YoY (fastest pace in ~5 years, beat ~$45.29B consensus) with operating income nearly doubling YoY to $17.8B, and a $578B backlog with >40% AWS growth guided for 2027-2028 -- confirming/strengthening the core cloud thesis. But EPS ($1.89) slightly missed (~$1.96-1.97 consensus) and trailing free cash flow collapsed to -$42.4B (from -$7.6B one quarter earlier) on a held $220B 2026 capex guide plus a flagged 'meaningfully' higher 2027 capex -- the same capex/FCF trade-off that hit GOOGL two days earlier. Shares fell ~7.3% after hours on the FCF/EPS miss despite the AWS beat. Return -7.6%. Position ~12.4%.

recent_transactions.rationale: ADD (corporate action, non-cash, not a watchlist-screened buy): Gentherm Incorporated (THRM) shares received as part of Modine's (MOD) Reverse Morris Trust spin-merger of its Performance Technologies segment into Gentherm, which closed 2026-10-01 (record date 9/28) -- 0.44619 THRM shares distributed per MOD share held. This was missed by prior daily reviews; discovered today while investigating MOD's continued price decline, which turns out to be substantially explained by the spin-off's value transfer (MOD dropped ~10% intraday on the 9/28 ex-date) rather than generic 'AI-data-center-adjacent/industrials weakness' as previously assumed. The retained Modine entity keeps the Data Centers/Commercial HVAC (Climate Solutions) business the original position's AI-cooling thesis was built on; Performance Technologies (lower-growth legacy automotive/industrial segment) is what was divested, so the retained MOD thesis is arguably sharpened, not broken. No official IRS Form 8937 cost-basis split was located; MOD's original $184.86/share cost basis was reallocated between MOD and these new THRM shares using the relative-fair-value method (first post-distribution regular-way closing prices on 10/1: MOD $189.21, THRM $31.56), yielding new cost bases of MOD $172.05/share and THRM $28.70/share -- see portfolio.json for detail. No cash impact (price shown is today's market price for reference only, not an acquisition cost). Token-sized (~0.05% of portfolio); doesn't move any sizing/sector/opportunity-bucket cap.

BUY: Astera Labs sourced from the 10/14 theme screen (AI data-center interconnect/connectivity silicon -- PCIe/CXL retimers and Scorpio fabric switches linking GPUs/CPUs inside AI server racks). Quant score driven by 104.5% revenue growth, 186.2% earnings growth, forward P/E 45.3 -- the top-ranked non-disqualified, non-opportunity-tier candidate on today's full watchlist screen (market cap ~$50.3B). Dedicated research check found no October-specific news, good or bad: the known customer-concentration risk flagged at the 10/14 add (top 4 customers ~82% of Q2 revenue per the Q2 10-Q) remains disclosed and stable, not worsening, and the stock's recent weakness reads as the broader sector-wide chip selloff (hitting CRDO/peers too) rather than a company-specific issue. Fundamentals intact: Q2'26 revenue $392M (>2x YoY, beat), Q3 guided to $540-560M (~40% QoQ). Passed on five higher-scoring candidates on this screen, each disqualified for a specific, dated reason: ASTS (still no news addressing the 10/13 Piper Sandler SpaceX-competitive-threat downgrade that triggered our 10/16 exit -- re-buy restriction stands), RCAT (CRO retaliation lawsuit from the 7/21 for-cause termination remains unresolved, no October update), SERV (Uber Eats non-renewal now confirmed executed -- Grubhub/DoorDash diversification is real but FY26 guidance cut to $9-10M stands, stock down ~45% over the past year), ZENA (a fresh October 2026 Form 424B5 offering at $1.35/share confirms, rather than resolves, the dilution concern flagged at the 10/14 pass), and IONQ (no news since 10/14 addressing the Elisity-deal/dilutive-raise strategic-drift concern behind our 10/14 exit; the ~35.8M new shares for Elisity, ~9% of shares out, confirm the dilution is material). Also passed on NVDA, which clears on fundamentals (105.9% revenue growth, 127.8% earnings growth, forward P/E 13.9, no negative catalyst found) but is the familiar mega-cap -- per the mandate against defaulting to blue chips over a smaller name the screen ranked higher without a specific reason, preferring ALAB here since nothing in the research disqualifies it. Not opportunity-tier; sized to the available cash above the 2% buffer floor ($54.16), the binding constraint today (ample remaining room in both the Technology sector cap and the 15% position cap).

SELL (thesis-breaking, not sizing): Piper Sandler downgraded AST SpaceMobile to Neutral from Overweight on 10/13, cutting its price target nearly in half to $54 from $98, specifically citing SpaceX's move to acquire low-band spectrum for a more aggressive Starlink Direct-to-Cell push -- a direct competitive threat to ASTS's core differentiated positioning as the first-mover satellite-to-phone carrier partner. Shares extended losses through 10/15-16 to a one-year low (~$40.66, -31.4% vs. cost basis), with coverage also citing six consecutive quarterly earnings misses, continued heavy cash burn, and newly publicized securities litigation alongside the already-known Pomerantz/Hunter/Delclaux suits. This is a new, concrete erosion of the original thesis -- a well-capitalized competitor entering the exact niche ASTS was priced on being first to -- not just beta-driven selling in the broader chip/CPI selloff hitting RKLB/SATL the same days. Fundamentals data (market cap, revenue/earnings growth) is unavailable this run -- yfinance's quoteSummary endpoint returned 401 Unauthorized/Invalid Crumb for all 91 tracked tickers today, a full fundamentals-API outage, not specific to this decision. Tiny position (~1.4%) -- a clean exit rather than holding a broken thesis at token size. Proceeds added to cash; no new BUY candidates could be screened today since scripts/evaluate.py's score_candidate requires fundamentals data unavailable in this outage.

BUY: Broadcom sourced from the standard watchlist screen (highest-ranked non-opportunity-tier, non-disqualified candidate; quant score driven by 85.5% revenue growth, 215.3% earnings growth, forward P/E 17.9). No fresh negative news found -- current weakness reads as a normal pullback (-29.5% June-Sept per Trefis 10/6) ahead of the December fiscal Q4 print, not a new catalyst. Passed on two higher-scoring opportunity-tier candidates on this screen: RCAT (CRO terminated "for Cause" 7/21, unresolved retaliation suit plus a separate pending securities class action and continued insider selling -- still disqualified) and SERV (Uber Eats relationship now confirmed effectively ending in early 2027 per the Aug 6/7 earnings call, and Uber has since sold its entire SERV equity stake -- disqualification stands, if anything stronger than before). Also passed on ZENA (no fresh red flag, but a persistent dilution/share-count concern -- 201M shares out per its 10/2 6-K -- a specific research-tied reason to pass rather than second-guessing the screen on familiarity grounds). Not opportunity-tier (~$1.65T market cap); sized to the available cash above the 2% buffer floor ($78.03), the binding constraint today, freed primarily by today's IONQ sale.

SELL (thesis-breaking, not sizing): IonQ announced an all-stock acquisition of cybersecurity firm Elisity worth up to $1.3B on 10/12 (shares fell ~9% specifically on dilution concerns), then priced a $2B equity offering (~$1.9B net proceeds) on 10/14, pushing shares down a further ~6% on that news alone -- distinct from and beyond the broader CPI/chip-sector selloff hitting peers (D-Wave -4.6%, Rigetti -4.9%, QUBT -5.1% same day). This is a real strategic pivot away from the original "quantum computing pure-play" thesis this position was added on, combined with material dilution (~$2B raise vs. a company with ~$280-290M revenue guidance) that the market has now independently and specifically punished twice. Not a sizing/cap-driven trim -- a clean exit on a broken thesis. Proceeds fund today's AVGO buy.

Passed on the higher-scoring opportunity-tier candidates on this screen -- RCAT (unresolved CRO retaliation lawsuit, insider selling and price downtrend both continuing/worsening) and SERV (FY26 guidance cut confirmed, plus a new and more severe detail: Serve says it is 'unlikely to renew' its anchor Uber Eats agreement in early 2027) -- and on HIMS (FTC suit and securities class-action both still active, lead-plaintiff deadline 11/2/26) and META (the 'Muse' rally has extended further into an unreported Q3 print, still a momentum-chasing entry). Not opportunity-tier (~$324B market cap); sized to the available cash above the 2% buffer floor (~$18.65), the binding constraint today, freed primarily by today's DUOL sector-cap trim.

Q2 2026 revenue $83.8M, +67% QoQ and >13x YoY, drove a raised FY26 guidance to $525-550M; pro forma backlog ~$757M after $175M of Q2 orders plus another $105M early in Q3, backed by $1.4B cash. Known quality caveat: ~92% of the recent revenue surge is acquisition-driven rather than organic, so this is sized conservatively (opportunity-tier, market cap ~$4.3B) to the remaining Technology sector-cap room (~$31.65, sector already ~29.2% of portfolio) rather than a full position, funded by available cash above the 2% buffer floor.

Trimmed the largest Tech holding (DUOL, ~14.5% position, itself near its own 15% position cap) back to bring the sector to ~29.8% -- a pure sizing rebalance; fundamentals (deliberate AI-feature reinvestment) and thesis unchanged.

Modine Manufacturing sourced from the 9/8 weekly theme screen (AI data-center liquid-cooling/thermal management). FY26 net sales +23% YoY to $3.2B, driven by a 90% increase in data-center cooling revenue, and the company signed a new long-term agreement this week to supply over $4B in cooling products through 2029 -- multi-year revenue visibility. Forward P/E 16.8 with 28% revenue growth and 44% earnings growth is a reasonable growth-at-a-reasonable-price setup versus richer AI-infra peers (e.g. RKLB's ~1,489x forward P/E, screened but passed on for this reason). Opportunity-tier (market cap ~$9.8B, just under the $10B threshold); sized to the full remaining opportunity-bucket room (~$23, bucket already ~19.4% of its 20% cap) rather than a full position, funded by available cash above the 2% buffer floor.

AST SpaceMobile sourced from the 9/8 weekly theme screen (direct-to-cell satellite connectivity). Shifting from proof-of-concept to commercial activation: BlueBird 11-13 satellites deployed, new New Zealand gateway opened, deepening carrier integration (Vodafone/Orange/Telefonica/Deutsche Telekom via a gateway JV) and US Mobile preparing a direct-to-cell launch. 2026 revenue guided to $150-200M (vs. a near-zero prior-year base, which drove the quantitative screen's outsized revenue-growth score), backed by a $1.3B backlog and over $3.7B cash funding the buildout. Key risk is execution on an expensive, tightly-timed deployment (implied ~165%/yr revenue growth needed through 2029), but the bull case is still considered intact by sell-side (~$78 fair-value estimate vs. ~$59.27 entry). Not opportunity-tier (~$23B market cap). Sized to the remaining Technology sector-cap room (~$81.65, sector already ~28% of portfolio) rather than a full position; funded by today's VRT trim proceeds.

First-ever stop-loss breach for VRT (-25.9% vs. cost basis at review), but unlike CRDO/INOD's chronic pattern this reads as a fresh, macro-beta-driven crossing -- Monday's broad AI-slowdown selloff hit Vertiv's ~2x-beta shares hard, and the stock was already recovering (~$234 on 9/15 toward ~$240 on 9/16). No earnings miss, guidance cut, or litigation; Q2 organic-growth guidance was actually raised to a 20-22% CAGR target through 2030, and sell-side remains heavily bullish (83% buy-rated, ~$341 average PT, GLJ upgrade to Buy $381). Trimming 30% to de-risk specifically because the 9/9 $1.45B UtilityInnovation Group acquisition still has undisclosed target financials and the Massachusetts data-center permitting order remains an unresolved overhang layered on top of the high beta -- not a full exit since there is no thesis-breaking catalyst.
